html:
The global security landscape is seeing a significant realignment today as the Saudi crown prince, Turkish president, and Pakistani prime minister formalized a joint defense pact in Mecca, with experts suggesting the agreement will profoundly alter the region's security dynamics amidst ongoing conflicts in the Middle East.

US Policy and Great Power Dynamics: In the United States, legislative and executive actions are shaping policy. The US Senate overwhelmingly passed the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia Act, aimed at punishing Russia and its petroleum buyers. Domestically, Trump is advancing efforts to restrict birthright citizenship, signing orders to tighten criteria and combat birth tourism. The White House also renewed efforts to remove Fed governor Lisa Cook despite a Supreme Court ruling. A federal appeals court halted construction of Trump's White House ballroom project, and political tensions are evident in the debate surrounding Todd Blanche's nomination for attorney general.

Middle East Security & Diplomacy: Significant diplomatic and security concerns focus on the Strait of Hormuz. Iran is reportedly nearing a deal with Oman regarding commercial shipping, with US officials expecting an agreement soon. However, Iran also aims to ban US and Israeli ships, a plan rejected by the Trump administration, and stated it would not allow a second corridor in Hormuz. Houthi rebels continue deadly attacks in Yemen, targeting the oil-rich Marib province and wounding civilians in Saudi Arabia, drawing regional condemnation. Meanwhile, Israel and Lebanon report progress in talks to verify Hezbollah disarmament, even as cross-border violence continues, with Israeli efforts to seize Palestinian land and new settlements reaching a "frenzied pitch" in the occupied West Bank. UNICEF reported 300 children killed in Gaza in 300 days.

Global Humanitarian & Security Crises: Humanitarian crises persist globally. The Democratic Republic of Congo is battling its largest Ebola outbreak on record, now surpassing 4,000 cases, exacerbated by active conflict. In Sudan, the besieged city of el-Obeid faces relentless drone strikes, critical water shortages, a cholera outbreak, and high rates of sexual violence, with the U.N. warning of mass atrocities. A tragic school shooting in Thailand saw a 14-year-old kill eight people, prompting the Thai PM to vow stricter gun laws.

European Migration & Internal Affairs: Migration continues to strain European relations. Spain imposed border controls on Italy, retaliating after Italy’s similar measures, following an influx of approximately 78,000 migrants from Morocco into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta. Elsewhere, Lithuania’s border guards discovered migrant tunnels from Belarus, which analysts view as a destabilization tactic. In the UK, communities in Thetford remain unsettled by "mob rule" linked to local frustrations over asylum plans.

Economic and Environmental Strain: Major tech company Meta has been ordered to pay $567 million and restrict some features for children in a US state court ruling, described as the largest child-safety judgment against the company. Environmentally, Puerto Rico has begun water rationing amid intensifying drought conditions, impacting hundreds of thousands. Droughts are also threatening power supplies in Danube countries like Hungary and Romania. Gold prices are on track for their largest weekly gains since January.
